moma:472.1941.title: The Starry Night
moma:472.1941.teaser: He painted it from a barred window in an asylum, the hills and the star are real, the village is not, and he thought it was a failure.

met:49.30.title: Cypresses
met:49.30.teaser: Painted the same summer, from the same asylum, and the tree he moved into The Starry Night stands here on its own.

aic:1942.51.title: Nighthawks
aic:1942.51.teaser: There is no door. Look for the way out of that diner and you will not find one, which is the whole painting.

met:57.92.title: Autumn Rhythm (Number 30)
met:57.92.teaser: He poured and flung the paint onto a canvas on the floor, the brush never touching it, and up close it is chaos. Step back and the whole wall begins to move.

met:JP1847.title: Under the Wave off Kanagawa (The Great Wave)
met:JP1847.where: The Japanese galleries, when it is on view
met:JP1847.teaser: The most famous wave in the world is a print the size of a placemat, and the small calm triangle it is about to swallow is Mount Fuji.

aic:1926.224.title: A Sunday on La Grande Jatte, 1884
aic:1926.224.teaser: Two years of tiny dots, no lines anywhere. Up close it is confetti, step back and a whole Sunday afternoon snaps into focus.

met:97.34.title: Washington Crossing the Delaware
met:97.34.teaser: Twelve feet tall and full of things that never happened, the flag not yet designed, the ice all wrong. It became the way a nation pictures its own founding anyway.

aic:1930.934.title: American Gothic
aic:1930.934.teaser: A farmer, a pitchfork, and a face the whole country has argued about since 1930. He meant it kindly. Nobody has ever been sure.

si-air:A19610048000.title: 1903 Wright Flyer
si-air:A19610048000.where: The Wright Brothers and the Invention of the Aerial Age, second floor
si-air:A19610048000.teaser: The pilot lay on his stomach and steered by sliding his hips, and everything this aircraft ever did, it did in one morning.

si-nmnh:G3551-00.title: Hope Diamond
si-nmnh:G3551-00.where: The Harry Winston Gallery, Janet Annenberg Hooker Hall of Geology, Gems and Minerals
si-nmnh:G3551-00.teaser: It is the size of a walnut, the blue is boron, and under ultraviolet light it glows red.

si-air:A19700102000.title: Apollo 11 Command Module Columbia
si-air:A19700102000.teaser: A three hundred and sixty three foot rocket left Florida and this twelve foot cone came back, and a laser scan in 2016 found the crew's handwriting still inside it.

si-nmah:star-spangled-banner.title: The Star-Spangled Banner
si-nmah:star-spangled-banner.artist: Mary Pickersgill, with Caroline Pickersgill, two nieces and Grace Wisher
si-nmah:star-spangled-banner.where: The Star-Spangled Banner chamber, second floor, off the central hall
si-nmah:star-spangled-banner.teaser: Count the stars and you get fourteen. The fifteenth was cut off and given away, and nobody today knows who has it.

nga:1967.6.1.a.title: Ginevra de' Benci
nga:1967.6.1.a.where: West Building, main floor, the Italian Renaissance rooms
nga:1967.6.1.a.teaser: The only Leonardo on public view in the Americas, and somebody sawed the bottom off it. Her hands are gone.

si-nmaahc:2009.50.39.title: Shawl Given to Harriet Tubman by Queen Victoria
si-nmaahc:2009.50.39.museum: National Museum of African American History and Culture
si-nmaahc:2009.50.39.where: Slavery and Freedom, the history galleries, Concourse level 3, when it is on view
si-nmaahc:2009.50.39.teaser: A queen invited her to the Jubilee, she did not go, and the lace came instead.

si-castle:smithson-crypt.title: The Crypt of James Smithson
si-castle:smithson-crypt.artist: Monument carved in Italy, unrecorded maker
si-castle:smithson-crypt.where: The small room immediately left of the north entrance, behind the iron gate
si-castle:smithson-crypt.teaser: He never once set foot in America, left it his whole fortune with no explanation, and the gate over his tomb is the fence from his grave in Genoa.

si-hmsg:picketts-charge.title: Pickett's Charge
si-hmsg:picketts-charge.where: Third floor, wrapping the inner ring
si-hmsg:picketts-charge.teaser: Eight canvases, nearly four hundred feet, wrapped around a round wall: an 1883 Gettysburg cyclorama buried under paper and then torn back open.

si-nmai:nnavm.title: National Native American Veterans Memorial, Warriors' Circle of Honor
si-nmai:nnavm.museum: National Museum of the American Indian
si-nmai:nnavm.where: Outdoors on the museum grounds, at the end of the curving stone path through the trees. Open at all hours, no ticket.
si-nmai:nnavm.teaser: Congress approved it in 1994 and nobody built it for twenty six years, and the cloths tied to the four lances were put there by visitors, who are invited to add one.

si-nmah:greensboro-lunch-counter.title: The Greensboro Lunch Counter
si-nmah:greensboro-lunch-counter.artist: F. W. Woolworth Company store fittings
si-nmah:greensboro-lunch-counter.where: Unity Square, second floor, west wing
si-nmah:greensboro-lunch-counter.teaser: The first Black customers served here were the store's own cooks, told to bring dressy clothes to work and change out of their uniforms first.

si-nmnh:USNM555000.title: The Nation's T. rex
si-nmnh:USNM555000.artist: Tyrannosaurus rex, found by Kathy Wankel, Montana
si-nmnh:USNM555000.where: The David H. Koch Hall of Fossils, Deep Time, ground floor
si-nmnh:USNM555000.teaser: It came out of the ground with the first complete Tyrannosaurus arm anybody had ever found, and the cast pieces on the mount are a different shade on purpose so you can see how much of it is real.

nga:1942.9.97.title: Woman Holding a Balance
nga:1942.9.97.where: West Building, main floor, the Dutch galleries
nga:1942.9.97.teaser: Everyone is told she is weighing gold. Look at the pans. They are empty, and that is the whole painting.

si-air:A19280021000.title: Spirit of St. Louis
si-air:A19280021000.artist: Ryan Airlines, designed by Donald Hall with Charles Lindbergh
si-air:A19280021000.where: National Air and Space Museum, National Mall. Galleries reopened in stages after the renovation and this aircraft has moved, so check the map at the door.
si-air:A19280021000.teaser: Walk to the nose and look for the windshield. There isn't one. He crossed the Atlantic seeing only out the side windows.

si-nmaahc:SC.0031.title: Southern Railway Car No. 1200
si-nmaahc:SC.0031.artist: Built by Pullman, partitioned by Southern Railway
si-nmaahc:SC.0031.museum: National Museum of African American History and Culture
si-nmaahc:SC.0031.where: Defending Freedom, Defining Freedom: Era of Segregation, history galleries, Concourse level 2
si-nmaahc:SC.0031.teaser: The segregated car you walk through. Pullman built it in 1922 with no partition, somebody welded that wall in eighteen years later, and two 500 ton cranes lowered it into this building three years before there were walls to stop them.

si-nmnh:A21128.title: The African Bush Elephant in the Rotunda
si-nmnh:A21128.artist: Mounted by William L. Brown with Norman Deaton; hide donated by Josef Fenykovi
si-nmnh:A21128.where: The Rotunda, ground floor, straight ahead from the National Mall entrance
si-nmnh:A21128.teaser: The tusks you are looking at are fiberglass, the real ones weigh ninety three pounds each, and the taxidermist went to the National Zoo to watch live elephants so he could get the walk right.

si-hmsg:belief-doubt.title: Belief+Doubt
si-hmsg:belief-doubt.where: Lower level. Ride the escalator down from the lobby. It covers the walls, the floor and the escalator sides, and runs on into the bookstore. Free, no ticket.
si-hmsg:belief-doubt.teaser: The largest artwork in the building is the one everyone walks over on the way to the bathrooms, and it is asking who is beyond the law.

si-nmai:prism-window.title: The Prism Window, Potomac Atrium
si-nmai:prism-window.artist: Charles Ross; design by Johnpaul Jones (Cherokee/Choctaw), from an idea of Donna House (Navajo/Oneida)
si-nmai:prism-window.museum: National Museum of the American Indian
si-nmai:prism-window.where: The Potomac, the round atrium just inside the east entrance. The window is in the south wall, on your right as you come in.
si-nmai:prism-window.teaser: Eight prisms in the south wall throw the spectrum in stacked bands across the atrium floor, and it only happens near the middle of a clear day.

si-nmah:1199660.title: Abraham Lincoln's Top Hat
si-nmah:1199660.where: The American Presidency: A Glorious Burden. Take a floor map at the door and go straight to it.
si-nmah:1199660.teaser: The Smithsonian was given it in 1867 and ordered its own staff never to show it or speak of it. The public did not see the hat again for twenty six years.

nga:1977.76.1.title: Untitled (the Calder mobile)
nga:1977.76.1.where: East Building, hanging in the atrium
nga:1977.76.1.teaser: Seventy six feet across and it weighs about as much as a motorcycle. In the steel Calder actually wanted, it would have weighed three tons and never moved.

si-nmaahc:2013.57.title: Cabin from Point of Pines Plantation
si-nmaahc:2013.57.artist: Built by enslaved carpenters, Edisto Island, South Carolina
si-nmaahc:2013.57.museum: National Museum of African American History and Culture
si-nmaahc:2013.57.where: Slavery and Freedom, history galleries, Concourse level 3, the lowest floor
si-nmaahc:2013.57.teaser: Sixteen feet by twenty, with nine to twelve people sleeping in the loft. It is not a reconstruction, and families were still living in it in the 1980s.

si-hmsg:66.4340.title: The Burghers of Calais
si-hmsg:66.4340.where: Hirshhorn Sculpture Garden, across Jefferson Drive from the museum building. The garden has been closed for a four-year rebuild and reopens 31 October 2026, with the Burghers among the works going back out. Free, no ticket.
si-hmsg:66.4340.teaser: Six men walking out to what they think is their execution, and Rodin refused to give them a hero, a pedestal, or a front to photograph.

si-nmai:americans-tomahawk.title: Tomahawk Missile, in Americans
si-nmai:americans-tomahawk.museum: National Museum of the American Indian
si-nmai:americans-tomahawk.where: Americans, the central gallery titled Indians Everywhere, third floor. Free, no ticket.
si-nmai:americans-tomahawk.teaser: A real flight test cruise missile carrying a Powhatan word, in the same room as the exhibition's Pocahontas gallery, and the curators refuse to tell you whether that is honor or trophy taking.

si-nmah:julia-childs-kitchen.title: Julia Child's Kitchen
si-nmah:julia-childs-kitchen.where: Food: Transforming the American Table, first floor, east wing. Walk the whole glass circuit, not just the first window.
si-nmah:julia-childs-kitchen.teaser: Her husband drew the outline of every pot on the pegboard, and built the counters two inches tall because she was six foot two.

si-air:A19510007000.title: Bell X-1 Glamorous Glennis
si-air:A19510007000.where: Boeing Milestones of Flight Hall, the main entrance hall
si-air:A19510007000.teaser: The last problem before the sound barrier was a door. With two broken ribs Yeager could not pull the hatch shut, so they cut down a broom handle.
